description.narrative: Chile is increasingly experiencing the impacts of climate variability and extreme hydrological events, ranging from prolonged drought spells to sudden and intense rainfall events that can result in flash floods, flooding and associated hazards. These contrasting extremes pose growing challenges for water resources management, disaster risk reduction and timely decision-making.The Chilean Directorate General of Water (DGA) has identified a need to strengthen the connection between hydrological data, modelling, earlywarning systems and operational decision-making, including the ability to translate available information into timely and actionable forecasts. The northern part of Chile has been identified by the DGA and the as a relevant area of focus, as the north experiences more extreme hydrological events.The DGA has a broad network of hydrological monitoring stations, datasets, studies and modelling tools. However, these sources are not yet fully integrated, and relevant information and modelling results are not consistently available online and in real time to support decision-making, particularly during rapidly developing events. In this context, Chile has expressed interest in technical assistance through the Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction & Surge Support (DRRS) programme, drawing on the Netherlands’ experience in integrated water management, land use, Early Warning Systems and Flood Forecasting.
